label: Person
name: Acácio Rodrigues Alves
summary:
Acácio Rodrigues Alves (1929–2012) was a Brazilian Catholic bishop who served in the Amazon region, ministering to indigenous communities and riverside populations in one of the Church's most challenging pastoral environments. Ordained a priest of the diocese of Santarém, he was consecrated bishop and spent the majority of his ministry in the vast Amazon basin of Pará state.

His episcopate coincided with accelerating deforestation, land conflicts, and the displacement of indigenous and riverine communities in the Brazilian Amazon during the 1970s–1990s. Like many Amazon bishops of his generation, Rodrigues Alves engaged these social issues as intrinsic to his pastoral mission, advocating for the territorial rights of indigenous peoples and the survival of traditional Amazonian ways of life. He participated in the REPAM (Red Eclesial Panamazónica) predecessor networks that connected Amazon bishops across national boundaries.

Rodrigues Alves represents the Amazon Church's distinctive pastoral theology—shaped by liberation theology, ecological concern, and the recognition that evangelisation must engage the totality of human experience. His ministry anticipated the concerns of the 2019 Amazon Synod, which addressed the same tensions between development, indigenous rights, and ecological preservation that defined his decades of service in the region.
